questions.question: State Hitler's three foreign policy aims and describe four steps he took between 1933 and March 1938 that broke or overturned the Treaty of Versailles.
questions.expected_answer: Aims: destroy Versailles, unite all German speakers in a Greater Germany, conquer lebensraum in eastern Europe. Steps: left the League of Nations and Disarmament Conference (1933); announced conscription and the Luftwaffe (1935); remilitarised the Rhineland (7 March 1936); formed the Rome-Berlin Axis and Anti-Comintern Pact (1936); annexed Austria in the Anschluss (March 1938).

questions.question: Explain the Munich Agreement and give three reasons why Britain and France followed a policy of appeasement, and one criticism of it.
questions.expected_answer: At Munich on 29 to 30 September 1938, Britain, France, Italy and Germany agreed that Germany would take the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia, which was not invited. Reasons: fear of another war like 1914 to 1918; belief that Versailles had been unfair; unready armed forces; fear of communism; economic weakness after the Depression; Dominions such as South Africa unwilling to fight. Criticism: it encouraged Hitler, made Germany stronger and was shown to have failed when he seized the rest of Czechoslovakia in March 1939.

questions.question: Explain how the Nazi-Soviet Pact led to the outbreak of World War II and describe how South Africa entered the war.
questions.expected_answer: The pact of 23 August 1939 removed the threat of a two-front war and secretly divided Poland, so Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939; Britain and France, having guaranteed Poland, declared war on 3 September, and the USSR invaded from the east on 17 September. In South Africa Hertzog proposed neutrality, but Parliament voted 80 to 67 for Smuts's motion on 4 September; Hertzog resigned, Smuts became prime minister and South Africa declared war on 6 September 1939.
